verdict.rationale: Steel has no native natural-language command interface of its own. It does ship first-party artifacts that let an AI agent operate it from natural-language instructions: an installable steel-browser skill plus the Steel CLI so 'your agent can control a browser' (steel-docs-12, steel-docs-8, steel-docs-34), and an in-process MCP tool exposure (steel-docs-9, steel-docs-46). The natural-language interpretation is done by the user's external agent or third-party Computer Use loops, not by Steel itself. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command surface in Steel itself, and hands-on or independent evidence that the skill-driven natural-language operation works well.
